text: In headless mode (`claude -p`), a conductor driver can launch the generated Workflow as a BACKGROUND task and then end its turn ('the run will notify me when it completes') — but ending the turn exits the -p process, killing the orphaned workflow. Observed live 2026-07-14 in an arena cell (uglify-corner-cases, opus-4-8[1m]/high): flawless Setup (DoD frozen, verify-reports.cjs grounded, per-report workers planned), then Workflow launched backgrounded, driver ended turn at ~17.5 min, process exited, wf/ branch left with ZERO commits, cell scored failed. Reproduced 2/2 on the same cell (attempts 1029s/1050s, both wf/ branches zero-commit); the same day five SHORT cells completed fine — the driver backgrounds the workflow precisely when it anticipates a LONG run, so the bug bites hardest on the hardest tasks. SKILL.md should pin the invocation: run the Workflow with run_in_background: false (or explicitly forbid ending the turn while the workflow runs — poll/wait until Finalize completes) whenever the session is non-interactive. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): SKILL.md (or the scaffold's driver instructions) contains an explicit run_in_background/do-not-end-turn directive for the Workflow invocation; today it says nothing, leaving the driver free to orphan the run.

Conductor loses to a RAW single session on wide, decomposable tasks because its generated plan runs independent work items as SEQUENTIAL phases. Measured head-to-head 2026-07-14 on arena task uglify-corner-cases (six INDEPENDENT compiler bugs, cellCapSec=3600): raw sonnet-5 one-shot RESOLVED 6/6 in ~53 min; opus-4-8[1m]/high + conductor TIMED OUT at 3603s with only 2/6 fixed — its driver designed Setup -> DoDBaseline -> Report1..Report6 -> DoDGate and paid worker spin-up + a ~5-min full-suite verification per phase, serially. The six reports were embarrassingly parallel (disjoint transforms, one shared file but separable hunks; a per-worker worktree already exists). SKILL.md / the scaffold should instruct: when the frozen DoD decomposes into independent criteria, fan the workers out concurrently (Workflow parallel()/pipeline over per-criterion workers, verify once at the gate), reserving sequential phases for genuinely dependent steps. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate a plan for a task whose DoD has N independent checkable criteria and assert the emitted loop runs their workers inside one parallel()/pipeline stage rather than N sequential phase() blocks; today the scaffold emits strictly sequential phases.

The --independent parallel fan-out (added by whetstone run conductor-20260714-182449) is unusable for the most common real shape of independent work: N independent changes that touch the SAME FILE. Proven live 2026-07-15 (true-v2 head-to-head, improved skill verifiably loaded via --plugin-dir): the driver read the new guidance, then correctly declined the flag — 'all six fixes touch lib/compress.js, so parallel editing would clobber' — because parallel workers share ONE worktree. SKILL.md's guidance ('no shared state') excludes shared-file tasks, so conductor stays sequential exactly where parallelism matters most (arena measured: sequential conductor times out at 3600s where a raw session resolves in ~53min). Fix: give --independent per-worker isolation — each parallel worker gets its OWN worktree/branch off the base, and a merge step (sequential rebase/cherry-pick with conflict-fix loop, or diff-level merge) combines them before the gates verify the combined diff once. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate with --independent and assert the emitted parallel workers are each instructed to work in a DISTINCT worktree (not the shared one) and that a merge/integrate step exists between the parallel Work phase and the gate; today all parallel workers share the single worktree and no merge step is emitted.

Even with SKILL.md pinning run_in_background:false + do-not-end-turn (kept fix from run conductor-20260714-182449, verifiably loaded), a headless opus driver STILL ended its run with the workflow unfinished: final message said 'I'm holding my turn open until the workflow finishes... Waiting for completion' and the -p process then exited at ~25min with only the setup harness committed (observed 2026-07-15, true-v2 cell). Saying it does not make it so: the driver must not emit a final text message at all while the workflow runs — the reliable pattern in -p mode is to invoke the Workflow tool with run_in_background:false so the TOOL CALL ITSELF blocks until completion, and SKILL.md should say exactly that (the tool call blocks; do not launch backgrounded and narrate waiting). Consider also instructing the driver to verify workflow status from .workflows/state/<name>.json AFTER the Workflow tool returns and before finalizing. Discriminating check is behavioral (claude -p A/B per the repo's proof norm): a headless run on a multi-phase task must end with the workflow state file status=complete/failed and a non-empty wf/ branch, not status=running; as a cheap structural proxy (RED now): SKILL.md's launch section must state that the foreground Workflow call blocks and that the driver must not end its turn with narration while status=running.

A judged-tier DoD criterion can be satisfied (or waved through as 'deferred') on the strength of worker reports alone. Observed live: spec required TOTP, DoDGate ran, the main agent relayed 'feature was deferred', and not a single line of TOTP code existed — the deferral was a unilateral scope change made by a step inside the workflow, and every report-reading layer confirmed it. Two-layer fix: (1) DoD acquisition (SKILL.md step 1c) should bias criteria toward the checkable tier by compiling them into executable checks (e.g. failing-first tests via lirbox-test-writer, RED at DoDBaseline) so 'deferred' is a red check, not a slippable status; (2) the DoDGate worker prompt for judged-tier criteria must require verification against the actual diff/artifacts in the worktree, explicitly treat worker reports/implementation-notes as untrusted claims, and hard-fail any criterion whose implementation was 'deferred'/'descoped' without a human decision recorded in the DoD file. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate a delivery workflow with a judged criterion and assert the emitted DoDGate prompt contains artifact-evidence + reports-are-untrusted + deferral-fails directives; today it has none of them.

When DoDGate finds unmet criteria after its 3 in-phase rounds, the generated conductor throws ('DoDGate failed: DoD not fully met') and the run dies — there is no outer verify-loop. The whole run's work is stranded one phase from done, and the only recovery is a human restarting. The generator should emit a bounded plan-execute-verify outer loop around Implement..DoDGate: on gate failure, a Replan phase receives the exact unmet criteria (ids + check output) and produces a new immutable plan version, execution re-runs, the gate re-runs; capped at N attempts (default 2); stall detection — if the unmet-criteria set is unchanged between two consecutive gate runs, stop early; every exit that is not gate-green escalates (state.json status 'escalated' with the unmet list and plan-version history) instead of throwing. Routing decisions must consume only executed check results, never worker reports. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate a delivery workflow and assert the script contains a replan/attempt loop with an attempt cap and an unchanged-unmet-set early-stop around the DoDGate, and that gate failure sets an escalated state rather than only throwing; today the gate is single-pass + throw.

--model-mode's default is backwards. `auto` (tier each worker by phase class: haiku for mechanical Setup/checkpoint/Verify/PR/TicketUpdate, the think model + effort:'high' for gates/RED/Writeup, the work model for --phases) is what we want on essentially every run, but it must be opted into — so real runs silently inherit the session model everywhere and pay a strong model on mechanical checkpoint/Setup/PR workers. Flip it: `auto` becomes the DEFAULT (no flag needed), and the old inherit-the-session-model behavior (emit NO `model:`/`effort:` opt at all) moves to `--model-mode inherit`. The literal `--model-mode default` must now HARD-ERROR pointing at `inherit` — keeping it as a silent alias would leave the flag value named 'default' meaning the non-default. The --model-think/--model-work guard inverts: they are valid with no mode flag (auto is default) and must be REJECTED under `--model-mode inherit`. Also update: the generator's stdout mode echo, references/generator-flags.md, SKILL.md, and scripts/snapshots/ (regenerate via test-scaffold.cjs --update-snapshots; renaming the misleading snapshots/default.js to inherit.js is fine). NOTE ON THE SURFACE: scripts/test-scaffold.cjs carries a 'default emits no model opt (byte-cost-free)' assertion pinning the OLD default — RETARGETING that assertion to pin `inherit` byte-cost-free is explicitly authorized and REQUIRED; deleting or weakening it is not. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): (a) generate with NO --model-mode flag and assert the emitted script carries model:'haiku' on Setup + checkpoint + PR, the think model with effort:'high' on CodeGate/RED, and the work model on the --phases workers; (b) generate with --model-mode inherit and assert NO `model:` and no `effort:` opt appears anywhere in the emitted script; (c) assert `--model-mode default` exits non-zero and its stderr names `inherit`; (d) assert --model-think with no mode flag exits ZERO while --model-think under --model-mode inherit exits non-zero. Today (a) emits zero model opts and (d) is exactly inverted.

The --independent fan-out is now mechanically sound (per-worker worktrees + integrate step, kept by run conductor-20260719-220515 / PR #34) but drivers still almost never pass it — observed 2026-07-25 across real usage: ~100% of generated workflows are strictly linear, no parallel() anywhere. This is a DECISION gap, not a mechanism gap. SKILL.md step 1b triages a tier and step 1c acquires a DoD, but NO step ever enumerates the work items or their dependency edges, and --independent survives only as a passive aside inside one paragraph of step 2 ('when the work items are independent, add --independent'). With sequential as the unstated default and no artifact forcing the question, the driver takes the linear path every time — which is exactly the shape arena measured losing to a raw single session on wide decomposable tasks (uglify-corner-cases: sequential conductor timed out at 3600s vs ~53min raw). Fix in SKILL.md: add a REQUIRED decompose step (a new step 1d, positioned BEFORE the generate step) in which the driver emits a work-item table with an explicit per-item 'depends on: <item ids | none>' declaration, plus the hard rule that every item whose dependency list is 'none' MUST be emitted in ONE --independent fan-out, with sequential --phases reserved for items carrying a declared dependency edge. Step 2's --independent paragraph must then reference that table instead of restating a soft heuristic, so the flag choice is read off a declared artifact rather than re-judged. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): assert SKILL.md contains a required decompose step that (a) names a per-item dependency declaration, (b) states a MUST rule binding no-dependency items to a single --independent fan-out, and (c) appears BEFORE the 'Generate the conductor' step; and that step 2's --independent paragraph cross-references it. Today SKILL.md has no decomposition step, no dependency declaration, and no MUST rule. NOTE: this is a structural proxy for a behavioral outcome — the real proof is an arena A/B of driver flag-choice across skill versions, currently blocked by arena's missing --plugin-dir/skill-version axis (filed separately in feedback/arena.jsonl).

The PHASE is conductor's unit of concurrency and a phase is exactly ONE worker, so work INSIDE a phase is always serial. Measured 2026-07-25 on a full delivery run: 16 agent() sites, only 2 parallel — and both fan out over a COMPILE-TIME constant (the CodeGate DIMENSIONS array). Nothing in a generated conductor ever fans out over a list a worker DISCOVERED at runtime. So a phase whose work decomposes into six independent files gets one worker doing them one after another, and no flag fixes it: --independent fans out PHASES, not work within a phase (and it is all-or-nothing — `--phases W1,W2,W3 --independent` emits a single parallel() of all three, so the mixed graph in SKILL.md's own 1d table, w1/w2 independent then w3 dependent, is not expressible). FIX: give each work phase a runtime planner + dependency-level fan-out. (1) For each work phase P the conductor first runs a PLANNER agent labelled `plan:

` returning { items: [{ id, title, prompt, dependsOn: [ids] }] } — decomposition happens at RUNTIME by a worker that has read the repo, not at scaffold time by an advisor guessing. (2) The conductor then fans the items out BY DEPENDENCY LEVEL: all items with empty dependsOn dispatch together in ONE parallel() batch, and an item dispatches only after every id in its dependsOn has resolved. This is pure JS over a worker-returned value, so it respects the conductor purity rule (no fs/git/Date.now/Math.random). (3) Each item worker gets its OWN worktree, reusing the per-worker isolation + integrate machinery already added for --independent. (4) The plan must be persisted for resume — the phase's checkpoint worker carries the item ids so a crash mid-phase reuses the plan instead of re-planning into a DIFFERENT decomposition than the commits already on the branch. (5) Default ON for work phases; `--no-plan-fanout` opts out to today's single serial worker. A plan with one item degenerates to today's behavior at the cost of one cheap planner round-trip (the planner is a think-class worker; --model-mode auto is now the default). Phase ORDER is untouched — this adds concurrency strictly inside a phase, so no existing sequential --phases semantics change. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): execute the emitted Workflow body with stubbed agent()/parallel()/phase(), answer the `plan:

` call with a fixed 3-item plan (w1,w2 independent; w3 depends on both), then assert a planner ran, one worker dispatched per PLANNED item (today: exactly one worker regardless of the plan), w1+w2 share one parallel() batch, w3 ran after them and outside that batch, each worker resolved to a distinct .worktrees/ path, and the phase checkpoint carried the item ids; plus --no-plan-fanout still yields a single planner-less worker.

conductor's SKILL.md has REGRESSED past skill-lint's 1200-word ● 'book' flag and is now the worst it has been since the original extraction. It was fixed once (2826 → 1479 words, check book-under-flag went GREEN and merged), then re-accreted monotonically across seven consecutive runs: 1479 → 1713 → 1833 → 2023 → 2146 → 2225 → 2469 (wc -w; skill-lint counts 2077 prose words vs its 1200 threshold). Nothing caught it because whetstone runs only the current run's items, so a kept fix decays invisibly — now fenced by the evals/checks-manifest.json floor guard, which records this as the one open 'red'. Cause is structural, not any single run: every whetstone item ADDS prose (guidance, rules, examples) and no step ever removes it; consolidate has been false on every run. FIX: relocate prose out of SKILL.md into references/ (progressive disclosure) until the body clears the flag — do NOT delete meaning, and do not just shuffle words between sections. skill-lint names the biggest section as the extraction candidate ('1c. Acquire the DoD', 458 w); the newer 1d decompose step and the frontend/content DoD probes are also relocation candidates — SKILL.md should keep the decision (WHICH tier/flag/step, and the hard rules) and reference/ should hold the HOW (the long-form probes, formats, and worked examples). The floor's 02-content-anchors test fences meaning-deletion, and the frontmatter description is the trigger and must stay specific. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): the existing evals/checks/book-under-flag.check.mjs — skill-lint must report NO finding with severity 'flag' + check 'book' for conductor. Pair this run with consolidate: true so the compress pass can also shrink the skill (kept only if the floor, every kept check, and the surface hold AND the skill strictly shrinks).

The CALLER should never decide how work is split — 'use conductor to implement this feature' must be the whole ask. Today conductor asks for the decomposition BEFORE anything has read the code: SKILL.md step 1d makes the advisor author a `depends on` table from a guess, and `--independent` turns that guess into structure. Both are the wrong layer. The runtime planner (kept by dynamic-fanout-within-phase) already derives items AND their edges from a worker that has read the repo, then dispatches by dependency level with each item's dependencies merged into its branch point before it starts. Principle to encode: the human declares the GOAL and the DEFINITION OF DONE (step 1c stays, human-confirmed); the LOOP decides the DECOMPOSITION. `--independent` has no surviving niche — a caller who wants a specific item list simply states it in the prompt and the planner returns those items; the flag only adds a way to be wrong, and it is unsafe when wrong: all `--independent` items branch off the SAME base and never see each other's output, so a mis-declared edge yields a CLEAN git merge over semantically broken code, with no runtime safety net (measured: 0 planner refs under --independent vs 35 on the default path). FIX: (1) reject `--independent` with a non-zero exit whose stderr points at the default planner path; (2) delete SKILL.md step 1d entirely — no caller-facing decomposition step, no `depends on` table; (3) state in SKILL.md that decomposition happens at runtime by the planner; (4) drop `--independent` from references/generator-flags.md as an offerable flag (a removal note naming it is fine); (5) keep `--no-plan-fanout` as the single escape hatch for forcing one serial worker, and keep `--phases` for genuinely staged human-declared stages (each phase gets its own planner) — this item removes the DECOMPOSITION instruction, not phases. Discriminating check (RED now, 3/6): evals/checks/loop-decides-decomposition.check.mjs. HUMAN PREP REQUIRED BEFORE RUNNING (evals/** is locked to the fixer): retire `independent-fanout-never-chosen` (asserts the very 1d MUST rule this deletes) and `independent-work-needs-per-worker-worktrees` (asserts a flag this removes) — otherwise the floor goes RED and the loop reverts the fix. Per-worker worktree isolation remains covered by dynamic-fanout-within-phase assertion 6, so retiring them loses no protection.

Cross-session resume trusts `args = { phasesDone, results }` without ever binding it to the SCRIPT that produced it. The generated conductor's entry guard validates only that phasesDone is a contiguous prefix of THIS script's phase order (scaffold-workflow.cjs, 'Resume reachability guard'), so any phasesDone whose titles happen to be a prefix of the new order is honored — and SKILL.md step 1 actively invites the divergence: the resume row says "regenerate (`--force`) only to change phase structure". Change --phases, --profile, --no-plan-fanout or any generator flag between runs and the stale phasesDone/results are applied to a DIFFERENT program: phases are skipped that this script never ran, and results keys are read back as if they came from the same code. The plan fan-out makes it concrete — a work phase reuses `results.<key>Plan.items` verbatim ('a resume never re-decomposes'), so a persisted decomposition is replayed into a script whose phase list, worktree layout or model tiers no longer match the commits already on the branch. grok-build makes this class of bug impossible: every host call is journaled with a SHA-256 request hash over the canonicalized payload, and a resumed script that issues a different call at the same sequence fails with JournalError::Divergence ('the workflow script is nondeterministic or was edited mid-run'); resume also re-executes the immutable REGISTERED script, never a regenerated projection, and rejects changed args outright ('workflow launch args are immutable across resume'). FIX (respects the conductor purity rule — pure comparison, no hashing at runtime): the generator injects a `const SCRIPT_ID = '<hash of the emitted body>'` constant at scaffold time; the checkpoint worker persists `scriptId` into state.json alongside phasesDone; the entry guard compares `args.scriptId` to SCRIPT_ID and, on mismatch, refuses to trust phasesDone/results/<key>Plan — it starts fresh (or throws with the two ids and an explicit override flag) instead of silently skipping phases. SKILL.md's resume row must stop presenting `--force` regeneration as compatible with an existing state file. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): generate a workflow, regenerate it with a different --phases list, then execute the SECOND emitted body with stubbed agent()/parallel() passing args.phasesDone/results (and scriptId, if emitted) captured from the FIRST — assert the run refuses the stale resume (fresh start or a throw naming both ids) rather than skipping phases; and assert the two generated scripts carry DIFFERENT SCRIPT_ID constants. Today no script identity is emitted or persisted at all, so the stale phasesDone is accepted and its phases are skipped.

The one status that means 'a gate says a human must decide' is written by the conductor and then destroyed by the skill. DoDGate persists `status: 'escalated'` plus the unmet-criteria list to state.json and then throws (kept fix from dodgate-replan-outer-loop) — but SKILL.md step 5 says to stamp status after the Workflow returns, "`failed`, not `complete`, if it threw", unconditionally. So the escalated marker is overwritten with `failed` on every escalation and the unmet list stops being the top-level signal. Worse, SKILL.md step 1's resume table only has rows for `running`/`failed` and `complete`: `escalated` matches NO row, so a run that stopped for a human decision has no defined resume motion at all. The taxonomy is also DoDGate-only — any other phase that needs a human (an ambiguous ticket, a design fork, a gate that legitimately cannot self-clear) can only throw, and reads as a crash. grok-build treats this as a first-class dimension: `pause(kind, msg)` takes user | back_off | no_progress | verification | infra, `verification` maps to a Blocked status, `is_resumable()` is a typed predicate over the taxonomy (all pauses plus Failed are resumable; Interrupted/Complete/Cancelled are not), and `await_user(kind, msg)` journals the question so a resumed run continues past it exactly once instead of re-asking. FIX: (1) the skill must never clobber a status the conductor already wrote — stamp `failed` ONLY when the persisted status is still `running`, so `escalated` survives the throw; (2) add an `escalated`/`blocked` row to the step-1 resume table that surfaces the unmet list / question to the human and resumes via the existing args path once they answer; (3) generalize past DoDGate — give the conductor a `blocked` terminal that persists `{ status: 'blocked', question, phasesDone, results }` and returns instead of throwing, so 'needs a human' is structurally distinct from 'crashed'. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): assert SKILL.md's finalize step conditions the `failed` stamp on the persisted status still being `running`, and that the step-1 resume table carries an `escalated`/`blocked` row; plus execute the emitted body with a DoDGate stub that never returns green and assert the persisted state still reads `escalated` (with the unmet ids) after the run's throw path. Today the stamp is unconditional and no resume row for `escalated` exists.

A dead item-worker in the plan fan-out is silently recorded as a COMPLETED item. `parallel()` resolves a worker that died after retries to `null`; the emitted level loop does `levelOut.forEach((r, i) => { itemResults.push({ id: level[i].id, title: level[i].title, summary: (r && r.summary) || '' }) })` — no .filter(Boolean), no ok flag, no count. The null becomes an empty-string summary pushed as a finished item, the level proceeds to integrate whatever branches happen to exist, and the phase result reports `'plan fan-out: N item(s) across M level(s)'` where N counts items that never ran. A phase where 3 of 5 workers died is indistinguishable, in state.json and to every downstream gate, from one where all 5 succeeded — and the run still terminates `complete`. The same swallowing applies to any per-item degradation: a plan item dropped by planItems (empty prompt, duplicate id), a dependsOn edge filtered as dangling, a cycle collapsed into one level — all are dropped or logged and then invisible in the durable state. grok-build's deep_research does the opposite as a discipline: every degradation (a question whose researcher failed, a claim excluded for missing evidence, an over-cap drop, a verifier shard that failed validation) pushes a line into `coverage_notes` and sets `partial = true`, and EVERY report ends with a 'Coverage and uncertainty' section — the run states which half worked instead of reporting binary success. FIX: record each item result as `{ id, title, ok, summary }` with ok=false for a null/failed worker; accumulate a run-level `coverage: []` note per degradation (dead item worker, dropped plan item, dangling dependsOn, cycle collapse, skipped gate, cap hit); carry `coverage` through checkpoint() into state.json; terminate as `status: 'partial'` (not `complete`) whenever any note exists; and have the Writeup phase render a 'Coverage and uncertainty' section from it. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): execute the emitted body with stubbed agent()/parallel(), answer ONE item worker inside a multi-item level with `null`, and assert (a) that item is not recorded as done with an empty summary — it carries ok:false, (b) a coverage note names its item id, (c) the terminal state status is `partial`, not `complete`. Today the null becomes `{ id, title, summary: '' }` and the run finishes clean.

The two control-flow decisions that gate the plan fan-out both hinge on a single self-asserted boolean from a worker. `levelSetup.ready` decides whether an entire dependency level is allowed to dispatch; `levelIntegrate.merged` decides whether that level's per-item branches are accepted into the run branch — and PLAN_SETUP_SCHEMA / PLAN_INTEGRATE_SCHEMA require only `ready: boolean` / `merged: boolean`. The conductor dispatched a KNOWN set (it built `itemBranches` and `itemWorktrees` from `level` itself) but never asks for that set back and never compares. An integrate worker that merged 2 of 3 branches and returned merged:true advances the run: the third item's commits never reach BRANCH, and every downstream gate (CodeGate, DoDGate, Writeup) then verifies an incomplete diff while reporting on the full plan. Note the asymmetry — the plan INPUT is already validated properly in pure JS (planItems dedups ids, drops dangling dependsOn, sanitizes slugs, degenerates safely; planLevels is cycle-safe and loud) — it is only the worker OUTPUT that is taken on trust. grok-build's deep_research shows the missing half: a verifier shard must return an exact BIJECTION on the claim ids it was handed (right count, every assigned id present exactly once, no id from outside the shard), checked in pure script at zero extra agent cost, and a shard that fails is discarded wholesale rather than partially believed. FIX: widen PLAN_SETUP_SCHEMA to require `created: string[]` (the worktree paths actually created) and PLAN_INTEGRATE_SCHEMA to require `merged_branches: string[]` (the branches actually merged); assert exact set equality against the dispatched sets before advancing; on mismatch, fail naming the missing/extra entries (and escalate per the blocked/escalated motion) instead of proceeding. Apply the same shape wherever a gate's routing decision reads a worker-reported boolean over a set the conductor already knows. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): execute the emitted body with stubbed agent(); answer the `<key>:integrate-l1` call with `{ merged: true, merged_branches: [<only 2 of the 3 dispatched branches>] }` and assert the run stops/escalates naming the missing branch instead of continuing to the next level or gate; same for `<key>:setup-l1` returning `ready: true` with a `created` list short of the dispatched worktrees. Today both schemas carry only a boolean, so the stub's `true` advances the run.

conductor ships its arena fixtures INSIDE its own skill directory: plugins/lirbox/skills/conductor/arena/tasks/<id>/{task.md,repo.bundle,grader/fail_to_pass/*.test.cjs}. Any mechanism that delivers the skill DIRECTORY to an agent as a payload therefore also delivers the hidden graders for all 9 tasks. VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY against Harbor 0.20.0: `harbor run --skill plugins/lirbox/skills` copies the tree into the container's $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/, which Claude Code enumerates at startup for skill discovery; the agent under test could read skills/conductor/arena/tasks/notes-add-tags/grader/fail_to_pass/10-store-tags.test.cjs — the answer key for the very task it was being graded on — plus every other task's graders, task.md and repo.bundle. A weaker form of the same exposure exists for an ordinary plugin install: an installed lirbox copy carries the same files on a filesystem a headless agent can read (reachable, but not in the discovery path, so lower severity). Note swe-grade.mjs's header claims F2P tests are injected `into a dir the agent never saw` — that is true of the INJECTION path only, and is not true of the skill/plugin payload. The scoring impact is that any run driven by a skill-injection mechanism is uninterpretable: a resolved cell cannot be distinguished from a cell that read the grader. FIX: move the arena fixtures OUT of the skill payload — e.g. to a repo-level evals/arena/ or plugins/lirbox/arena/ — and point conductor/arena/suite.json at the new location; nothing shipped as skill content should contain grader/fail_to_pass/ or a fixture bundle. An interim mitigation already exists for the Harbor path only (scripts/harbor-port.mjs prunes conductor/arena/ and *.bundle out of the injected catalog and hard-fails if any grader survives the prune), but that guards one consumer, not the packaging defect. DISCRIMINATING CHECK (RED now, GREEN after): walk the conductor skill payload — the tree a skill-injection mechanism would copy, i.e. plugins/lirbox/skills/conductor/ — and assert it contains zero files matching grader/fail_to_pass/*.test.cjs and zero *.bundle files. Today that walk finds 38 grader files and 9 bundles and the assertion fails; after the fixtures move it finds none.

The plan fan-out's per-item worktree setup reuses a stale branch WITHOUT rebasing it, which turns one integrate conflict into a deterministic infinite retry. scripts/prompts/setup-item-worktrees.txt has three arms; the fresh arm is correct (`git worktree add "$WT" -b "$BR" "${BRANCH}"` -- every item in a level forks off the SAME base, the run branch tip), but the reuse arm is `elif git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$BR"; then git worktree add "$WT" "$BR"` -- it adopts the branch wherever it was last forked, and never checks whether ${BRANCH} has moved since. It always has. Concrete loop: level 1 integrates, so BRANCH advances T0 -> T1; level 2 forks off T1; one item conflicts, and integrate-items.txt step 4 DELIBERATELY keeps the conflicted branch ('keep any UNMERGED (conflicted) branch so its work is not lost') and returns merged=false, so the phase throws. On resume the plan is reused verbatim (results.<key>Plan), level 1 re-runs and re-merges, BRANCH advances T1 -> T2 -- but level 2's surviving branch still points at T1. setup_item takes the reuse arm, hands the worker a tree forked two integrations back, and integrate hits the SAME conflict. Every resume widens the gap between the stale fork point and BRANCH, so the run cannot converge: it fails identically forever while spending a full level of workers per attempt. Note the diagnosis this masquerades as -- it LOOKS like items branching from different bases (uat vs main), so a 'make every item share a base' fix is a no-op; the bases are already shared, it is the reuse path that skips the rebase. Related: --base is only read by the Setup phase, and Setup is skipped on resume, so the run's base ref is also silently frozen after the first launch even though args.base looks live. FIX: in setup_item's reuse arm, classify the existing branch before adopting it -- if `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$BR" "${BRANCH}"` (already fully merged) then delete it and take the fresh arm so the item re-forks off the current tip; otherwise `git rebase "${BRANCH}" "$BR"` to move its unmerged work onto the current tip, and if that rebase conflicts, abort it and report ready=false naming the branch so the run ESCALATES (a human decision) instead of dispatching a worker onto a doomed base. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): assert the emitted setup-item prompt text contains a merge-base/ancestor classification and a rebase (or delete-and-refork) of an existing item branch before `git worktree add "$WT" "$BR"`, and that the reuse path can return ready=false; today the prompt's reuse arm adopts the branch unconditionally and the only ready=false path is a missing directory.

The plan fan-out persists the PLAN but never the PROGRESS, so any failure re-dispatches every level from 1. In scaffold-workflow.cjs planFanoutBody() the only checkpoint inside a work phase fires once, right after decomposition (`results.<key>Plan = { items }` then `await checkpoint('<Phase>')`, guarded so 'a resume never re-decomposes'). The `for (let li = 0; li < levels.length; li++)` loop that follows writes NOTHING durable: itemResults accumulates in memory, and `results.<key> = { summary, items: itemResults }` lands only after the last level returns. So a level-3 integrate failure discards levels 1-2 entirely -- on resume the phase re-runs setup, re-dispatches every level-1 and level-2 worker, and re-integrates work whose commits are ALREADY on BRANCH. The workers are pointed at a base that already contains their output, so they either no-op (pure waste) or re-apply the change (duplicate edits, then a conflict). This is the dominant token cost of a failed fan-out phase, and it compounds with stale-item-branch-reused-across-resume: each retry pays for the whole phase AND still hits the same unrebased conflict, so the spend per attempt is constant and the outcome never changes. The phase-level `done` set cannot express this -- its granularity is the phase, and the fan-out's real unit of progress is the dependency level. FIX: checkpoint after each level's integrate succeeds, recording per-item outcomes not just a high-water mark: `results.<key>Levels = [{ level: <n>, items: [{ id, ok, summary }] }]`, written via the existing checkpoint worker. Guard the level loop on it (`if (results.<key>Levels?.some(l => l.level === li + 1)) { log('level N already integrated (resumed)'); continue }`) so a resume skips fully-integrated levels, and when a level is re-entered, re-dispatch ONLY items whose recorded ok is false. The per-item `ok` flag is the same field dead-item-worker-recorded-as-done needs for a null worker, so land them together rather than adding two overlapping shapes. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): execute the emitted work-phase body with a stubbed agent() over a 2-level plan; answer level 1 setup/work/integrate successfully and make level 2's integrate return merged=false, then re-execute with the resulting results object as prior and assert the level-1 work agents are NOT called a second time. Today nothing about level 1 survives in results, so the resumed run re-dispatches it in full.

Every retry bound in conductor is scoped to ONE gate invocation, and nothing bounds the number of invocations -- so a permanently-failing phase burns unlimited tokens across relaunches. gateLoop(), panelBody()'s lead loop, frontendBody()'s per-target loop and TestGate all run `for (let round = 1; round <= 3 && !passed; round++)` and then `throw`; DoDGate adds an outer DOD_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2 with stall detection. All of those counters are LOCAL variables in one workflow execution. The durable state schema (references/workflow-runtime.md) has no attempts field, and SKILL.md step 5 stamps `failed` on a throw precisely 'so a later resume re-runs only the failed gate' while step 1's resume table treats `failed` as an unconditional resume row. So the caller relaunches, the phase is not in phasesDone, its 3 rounds run again from zero, it throws again -- and the state after attempt N is byte-identical to the state after attempt 1. The loop has no memory, so nothing can ever decide to stop; the operator only finds out by watching spend. The conductor also never reads the Workflow `budget` global, so there is no second-order cap either. Note this is distinct from escalated-status-clobbered-and-unresumable: that item is about the status TAXONOMY surviving the skill's finalize stamp; this one is about there being no COUNTER to escalate on in the first place, and it applies to every gate, not just DoDGate. FIX: (1) add `attempts: { '<Phase>': <n> }` to the durable state schema, carried through args on resume alongside phasesDone/results; (2) in the emitted phase skeleton (emitPhase), increment the phase's counter and checkpoint it BEFORE running the body, so a crash mid-phase still costs an attempt and cannot be reset by relaunching; (3) when `attempts[P] >= PHASE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 3), do not run the body -- persist `status: 'escalated'` plus the phase name and the last gate summary, and throw naming the cap; (4) add an `escalated` row to SKILL.md step 1's resume table that STOPS and surfaces the reason to the human instead of relaunching, and make step 5 never overwrite a status the conductor already set. The brake must live in durable state, not in the workflow body -- a counter that resets on relaunch is exactly the bug. Discriminating check (RED now, GREEN after): execute the emitted body with a stubbed agent() whose CodeGate lead always returns gatePassed=false, catch the throw, feed the resulting state back as resume args, and repeat; assert that by the 4th launch the phase's agents are NOT dispatched at all and the persisted status is 'escalated'. Today every launch re-runs the full 3 rounds and re-persists an identical state, indefinitely.
